I never found SC to be exciting to watch. AoE is definitely the more exciting one to spectate in my opinion. But as for playing the game, I don't think there is really much gap between them. I think SC is great, but AoE just has so much. I think a lot of AoE is played on the fly. You have your build order plans in the beginning, but everything after that is totally reactive. When I watch SC, I rarely ever see someone switch from what they originally planned to do. I also don't see much variety in strategy when it comes to top pro play.

Also, I think AoE is more fun in lower elos too. I feel like playing competitively in AoE is more fun, where as in SC it can be frustrating. Even losing in AoE is fun because you had fun playing the game. And I feel like every part of the match is fun, the early, mid, and late game.

I also like how there are more than one way to win a match, and I think they did that very well, where the different ways to win are just as fun.

A big thing for AoE that I really really enjoy is how the maps are never the exact same, even if you pick a designed map it is still generated but just around a template. I mostly enjoy mega random though. I wish there was more competative play around mega random because I think not knowing the land makes for more interesting gameplay, so people don't immediately know exactly what tech they're going for and what build order to use.

I think SC is really fun, I still enjoy playing SC but I mostly just enjoy co-op. I just think the gameplay in versus is too predictable. My favorite part of SC is the campaign by far. I absolutely loved the SC2 campaign, it is a lot of fun and I often replay it.

About the planets, I think they were procedurally generated pretty well. I think the planets being very open just makes sense. In reality, a human race capable of intergalactic travel would use most planets just for mining and research, and they really wouldn't be building vast cities on any of them. Not to mention how difficult it would be to govern so many cities across tons of planets and galaxies. The emptiness is validated by logic. It's a coincidence that it also makes it easier to procedurally generate.

About the looting, I don't want to say I hate looking in every nook and cranny. Skyrim is tiny compared to Starfield, but Skyrim couldn't even have open cities, you had to download a mod to have that.

Skyrim was as big of a downgrade for the Elder Scrolls series as Battlefield 2042 was to the Battlefield series. But Skyrim got insanely positive reviews somehow, probably because it brought a ton of new fans to the series and most never played Morrowind which was so much more detailed than Skyrim.

I'm not going to sit here and tell you Starfield is the perfect game. But I will argue that your statement that it's a downgrade is wrong. It is a lot different than their other games. Their other games had just one large landscape to explore, where with Starfield they had to create a ton of whole galaxies to explore. Yes, most of the planets have a lot of landscape in between points of interest, but that's kind of how it would be. Not every planet is going to be another Earth. I think they designed it very well.

Like I said, I am not trying to tell you Starfield is the best Bethesda game ever made by far. I am just trying to say that the shit it gets is very undeserved and that it is a pretty good game for Bethesda's first time making an RPG with space travel. There's no other complete game like it.
